answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards; peers slash that stake when a challenge reveals duplicated credentials or fabricated work. One operator can still mint many keys, but must immobilize capital for every one and risks losing it, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free. A walnut-sized deposit is not enough if rewards are large; calibrating the bond to expected gains matters. A relic credential or prism-shaped avatar adds no protection unless tied to that enforceable stake.
